Referral Note

30-year-old emergency department nurse with five ED visits over the past four months for sudden episodes of chest pain and shortness of breath. Episodes begin without warning, with intense fear, palpitations, sweating, trembling, nausea, dizziness, chest tightness, and a conviction that she is dying. Symptoms peak within approximately 10 minutes and resolve over the following 30. She has developed persistent fear of further attacks and now avoids grocery stores, shopping malls, movie theaters, and waiting in lines, anticipating she could not escape if symptoms began. Cardiac evaluation, including serial ECGs, Holter monitoring, stress testing, and laboratory studies, is unremarkable. Referring for psychiatric evaluation and treatment planning.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately dressed and groomed. Appears stated age.

Behavior: Cooperative throughout. Becomes visibly anxious when describing her symptoms; checks her own radial pulse twice during the interview.

Speech: Normal rate and volume.

Mood / Affect: Describes mood as “scared this is going to happen again”; affect anxious and congruent.

Thought / Perception: Logical and organized. Content centers on fear of recurrent attacks and of undetected cardiac disease. No delusions or hallucinations. Denies SI/HI.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and oriented. Insight fair: she acknowledges the workup was negative while remaining doubtful. Judgment intact.
